newsitem.title: USA: Let FASB finish derivatives rules, Levitt urges.
newsitem.headline: Let FASB finish derivatives rules, Levitt urges.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt Tuesday urged the business community not to use outside influence to deter an accounting body from setting derivatives accounting rules.

Speaking before a gathering of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, Levitt voiced support for the work of the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) which has set a June 30 deadline for finishing the rules.
Levitt said it has been his policy to find solutions to difficult problems by consensus, "avoiding going outside the process by passing a new rule or asking Congress for a new law," he said.
"I expect similar respect for the preocess from you and all the members of the business community," he said.
At issue is a proposal by the FASB, the Norwalk, Conn.-based private group that sets accounting standards for U.S. corporations. The SEC has oversight over the body.

The body's hotly debated proposal calls for companies and banks to include derivatives -- financial contracts whose value is linked to the price of an underlying asset such as a stock, commodity or currency -- in their financial statements and not off balance sheet.
A slew of big companies are opposed to the proposal, saying it could result in excessive volatility to their earnings.
In backing the FASB, Levitt noted that the body's procedures, with public participation and SEC oversight, insure there are opportunities for stakeholders to express their views.
"The process requires meaningful, constructive, and well-supported input, with participants looking beyind immediate interests..." he said.
"With those cautions in mind, I encourage all of you to involve yourselves in the standard-setting process," he added.
